paragraphs: The daily rhythm is coach, train, record, and protect. In the morning, receive scheduled patients and guide stretching, strength, and balance work while observing expressions and exertion, then record results. In the afternoon, operate therapy devices and help patients transfer and walk. Long-term patients return daily, accumulating progress little by little; the body gets tired while the work warms the heart.

The role also depends on the physical therapist practice system, creating a clear assistant-level ceiling that requires continued certification and advancement.
